ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure shows a two-transistor current mirror circuit, with a 15 V power supply on the right connected between the upper and lower power rails. The emitters of the two transistors are connected to the upper power rail, and their bases are connected together. The left transistor is the reference branch, and the left node is also connected to the lower power rail through a resistor labeled 2.2 kΩ; the output branch of the right transistor is connected with a variable R_load to the lower power rail. Reasoning: According to the silicon transistor base-emitter forward voltage drop given in the problem, it is about 0.7 V. The left reference transistor makes the common base/collector node about 0.7 V lower than the +15 V emitter potential, so the voltage across the 2.2 kΩ resistor is about 15 - 0.7 = 14.3 V. The reference current I_ref = 14.3 V / 2.2 kΩ = 14.3 / 2200 A ≈ 0.0065 A = 6.5 mA. The current mirror will make the current in the right R_load branch approximately equal to this reference current, so the load current is about 6.5 mA.

method.method_draft: From the image, note that the left transistor sets the reference current through the 2.2 kΩ resistor from the common base/collector node to the bottom rail. Use the text-given silicon drop: the common base node is about 0.7 V below the +15 V emitter rail, so the resistor has approximately 15 - 0.7 = 14.3 V across it. Compute I_ref = 14.3 V / 2.2 kΩ ≈ 6.5 mA. Since the right transistor mirrors this reference current, report the current through R_load as approximately 6.5 mA.
